sights.w: One of Singapore's largest heartland parks and a global model for river restoration — under the ABC Waters Programme, a 2.7 km concrete stormwater canal was torn out and rebuilt as a 3 km meandering naturalised Kallang River. A 2017-19 NUS study found the naturalised river lifted the park's biodiversity by 33% (197 animal species, incl. 59 birds and 22 dragonflies).

sights.address: Block 159A, Ang Mo Kio Ave 5 (foot of Ang Mo Kio Town Garden West), Singapore
sights.w: Singapore's largest bird-singing and display arena — established 1987 from a 1970s gathering of three AMK zebra-dove keepers, it holds more than a thousand cages on 20-foot poles rigged with pulleys across a space the size of two football fields. A rare surviving fragment of kampong-era culture and a stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.

sights.n: Ang Mo Kio Town Garden West
sights.address: Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 / Avenue 6 (opposite Ang Mo Kio Public Library), Singapore
sights.w: Completed in 1983 as the HDB's largest town-garden project of its day (~21 ha), built on a hillock with spreading greenery, a lotus pond home to some 19 dragonfly species, and a lookout — a pioneering piece of heartland landscaping and an Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail site. (Note: a section near the pond is affected by LTA's North-South Corridor works.)

sights.n: Ang Mo Kio Town Garden East
sights.address: Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 / Avenue 8 (behind Ang Mo Kio MRT), Singapore
sights.w: The eastern counterpart town garden, tucked behind Ang Mo Kio MRT at the junction of Avenues 3 and 8 — a landscaped neighbourhood green with ponds and rest areas serving the surrounding HDB blocks.

A 75-ha nature park opened in 2017 on the AMK/Upper Thomson fringe, a quieter gateway into the Central Catchment. About 4 km of trails — the boardwalked Hanguana Trail over a freshwater swamp forest, the Venus Loop and Drongo Trail — link to MacRitchie and the TreeTop Walk.

sights.address: Central Catchment Nature Reserve (via Venus Drive, off Upper Thomson Road), Singapore
sights.w: A 250 m free-standing suspension bridge strung between MacRitchie's two highest points, Bukit Peirce and Bukit Kalang, high in the rainforest canopy — reached on foot from the AMK-side Venus Drive / Windsor trailheads. Closed Mondays (except public holidays).

sights.address: Casuarina Road / Upper Thomson Road, Singapore
sights.w: A park around Singapore's second-oldest reservoir (1910s) whose 900 m nature boardwalk, built in 1998 along existing trails, threads one of the island's last mature secondary forests at the water's edge — home to more than 900 flowering plants, 100 ferns and 250 animal species.

Singapore's 7th nature park (opened 2019), built around the atmospheric ruins of a 1930s-60s Hainanese village and a key conservation site for the critically endangered Raffles' banded langur. Five trails (3.8 km) — Ruins and Figs, Stream and Ferns, Rambutan, Langur and Macaque — wind past old village foundations and troops of long-tailed macaques.

sights.address: Ang Mo Kio Town Centre (trail markers islandwide across AMK), Singapore
sights.w: NHB's self-guided trail through Singapore's quintessential heartland town — refreshed in 2023 to 40 heritage sites and 10 markers across three routes (Iconic Landmarks, Hidden Heartland Gems, Scenic Fringes), linking the Clover Block, Kebun Baru Birdsinging Club, Chu Sheng Temple, Church of Christ the King, Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park and more.

The only Catholic church in Ang Mo Kio — its foundation stone laid in 1981 by Archbishop Gregory Yong, it cost around S$3 million (then twice any other church in Singapore) and opened in 1982 before being rebuilt in 2002. Marked on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail; the facade carries a statue of Christ the King.

The only block of circular flats the HDB ever built — four round towers joined into a four-leaf-clover plan (completed 1981), part of a late-1970s pilot of seven distinctively designed blocks meant to give estates their own identity. Built in solid brick with round rooms larger than a standard five-room flat; now an AMK icon and a heritage-trail marker.

A Hokkien-style temple built in 1981 to house three older village temples — Ji Fu Gong, Hua Tang Fu and Long Quan Yan — displaced from Yio Chu Kang's 11th milestone (Ka Tau Au) by redevelopment. Pronounced curved roof ridges mark its Hokkien architecture; former villagers still gather here and it runs community charity. An Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem.

Ang Mo Kio's HDB-built neighbourhood mosque, opened 21 September 1980 for a community that had earlier prayed at Thomson Road and Kampong Sireh. Part-funded by MUIS with the rest raised by residents through donations and food fairs, it accommodates up to 3,500 worshippers and is a marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.
